h1:
Chumphon Coffee Trip
From Robusta Farms to City Cafes
intro: Chumphon is Thailand's biggest robusta-growing province, but plenty of people drive straight through on their way to the Koh Tao ferry without realising there are coffee farms set right in the orchards where you can watch the roast, plus city cafes pouring local robusta for less than you'd pay in a big city. This 2-day plan is built for coffee people. Day one heads up to the farms around Pathio and Tha Sae, from cherry-laden trees to the roaster; day two loops the city cafes and finishes by the sea at Pak Nam. We've put in real shops, real opening hours, and rough prices so you can tweak it to suit yourself.
chips: 🌿 cafes set in the coffee farms

blocks.html: The fun of a coffee trip in Chumphon is getting to see the whole cycle: from red coffee cherries on the tree, to the drying beds, to the roaster filling the whole shop with that smell, finishing with a cup pulled from the same batch. Then there are the city cafes, where a younger generation has come home to make specialty coffee from their family farms. So this plan splits cleanly into two days, a farm day and a city day, because the growing areas sit outside town in the opposite direction from the cafes. Trying to cram it into one day means too much tiring back-and-forth driving.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Most of Chumphon's coffee farms are small family orchards with tiny cafes, not ticketed attractions. Some close on weekdays, and roasting isn't on show every day. If you want to actually watch a roast or pick cherries, message the shop's page first to ask about timing, and double-check their day off, since several cafes on this list close on different days.

blocks.text: The 2-day coffee plan at a glance

blocks.html: Day one is the farm day: drive out of town and head north to Pathio and Tha Sae, the main growing areas. You'll sit at cafes in the orchards, look at the drying beds and the roast, then buy beans straight from the farm to take home. Day two is the city day: loop the renovated old-house cafes and slow bars in town through morning and afternoon, then close out by the sea at Pak Nam in the evening. The rhythm works whether you drive in yourself or arrive by train or plane and rent a car in town.

items: Day 1 — Farm day around Pathio and Tha Sae: watch the roast, taste local coffee, buy beans at the source
Day 2 — City cafe-hopping that runs all the way to the seaside at Pak Nam
Where to base yourself — in town in Chumphon, near the cafes and market, with an easy drive up to the northern farms

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Farm day around Pathio and Tha Sae: watch the roast, taste local coffee

items.activity: Start the morning in town with a hot local robusta alongside breakfast before heading up to the farms
items.note: Fuel up before the drive, since the farms are out of town

items.activity: Drive out to Fly Robusta at Ban Chong Mut, Pathio district, and sit at a cafe set in a working coffee farm
items.note: There's a tree-house corner that photographs well, coffee brewed from beans grown on site. Open Fri–Sun, closed Thursdays

items.activity: Move into the Tha Sae area, Chumphon's main growing zone, and stop at Coffee Travel
items.note: If you've arranged it ahead, you can watch the roast and try making coffee step by step

items.activity: Break for lunch at a local spot around Tha Sae and try some bold southern Thai food
items.note: Fuel up before the afternoon community-farm visit

items.activity: Visit the community coffee farms around Tha Sae and Phato, with drying beds and a roasting house (book ahead)
items.note: Harvest runs roughly December to February; some farms let you try picking cherries

items.activity: On the way back to town, stop at Robusta Station on Phetkasem Road for beans and souvenirs
items.note: Open daily, with roasted coffee, southern curry paste, and dried fish to take home

items.activity: Head back to your place in town, rest up, and save your energy for tomorrow's cafe-hop
items.note: Keep your beans somewhere dry, and don't grind them until you're ready to brew

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: City cafe-hopping that runs all the way to the seaside at Pak Nam

items.activity: Start the morning at Comienzo House, a renovated old-house cafe in the Na Thung neighbourhood
items.note: First cup with house-made cake; photograph the old house before it gets busy

items.activity: Move on to Morning Drug Cafe, a minimal white-toned cafe surrounded by greenery
items.note: Try the house-made croissant; there's a co-working corner if you want to stay and work

items.activity: Lunch in town: bold southern Thai food or a rice-and-curry plate
items.note: Settle your stomach before the afternoon cup

items.activity: Carry on to specialty coffee at BEEN BARISTORY, strong on both hand-picked coffee and matcha
items.note: Grab the beach-chair corner or a window seat for photos

items.activity: Stop by Panich Coffee and Roaster and talk robusta with the roaster himself
items.note: An old-wood cafe that roasts its own organic beans, good for anyone who wants to go deep on the beans

items.activity: Finish at Rolly Cafe, a slow bar by the sea at Pak Nam, sipping self-roasted coffee in the breeze
items.note: Closed Tuesdays, so check before you go; parking is tight, so get there a little early in the evening

blocks.title: If you've only got half a day
blocks.html: If you're passing through Chumphon on the way to the islands and short on time, just keep three stops in town. Start at S.C. Farm Fine Robusta in the Nong Yai Rat area, which has a coffee field close to town, then Panich, which roasts its own in town, and finish at Robusta Station on Phetkasem Road to grab souvenirs before you carry on. Half a day still gets you the coffee trees, a taste of local coffee, and beans to take home.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Chumphon trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Chumphon
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: The cafes and farms in this plan that you can actually visit

blocks.html: These are picked from places that are open and getting steady reviews, ordered from the orchard farms outside town inward to the city and seaside cafes, following the order you'd likely hit them across these two days. It isn't a ranking of which shop beats which. Opening hours can shift, so check the shop's page again before you head out.

items.name: Fly Robusta (Ban Chong Mut, Pathio)
items.blurb: A cafe set in a coffee farm at Ban Chong Mut in Pathio district, where you sit among real coffee trees. There's a photogenic tree-house corner, coffee brewed from beans grown on the farm, and house-made bakery. It's a bit far from town, but reviewers say it's worth the drive, and it makes the perfect start to the farm day.

items.name: Coffee Travel Tha Sae
items.blurb: A cafe in Tha Sae, Chumphon's main coffee-growing area. At certain times it runs coffee-making classes and lets you watch the roast step by step, so it's good for anyone who wants to learn rather than just sip. If you want to catch a workshop, message the shop's page first to ask about timing.
items.meta: Tha Sae · coffee activities at certain times

items.name: Tha Sae–Phato community coffee farms
items.blurb: Several villages around Tha Sae and Phato have banded together into community coffee enterprises. Some open up their drying beds, fermentation, and roasting rooms, and let you try picking cherries during harvest. It's an off-the-radar side of Chumphon that few people reach, and you'll need to book ahead through the community group.

items.name: S.C. Farm Fine Robusta Chumphon
items.blurb: A robusta coffee field in the Nong Yai Rat area of Mueang district, close to town, where you can walk the coffee plots without driving far. There's a cafe serving coffee from the farm, ideal for anyone short on time who still wants to see the trees.
items.meta: Mueang Chumphon (Nong Yai Rat) · close to town

items.name: Robusta Station
items.blurb: A cafe and souvenir stop on Phetkasem Road, on the way out of town toward Bangkok. Open morning to evening daily, and besides coffee it stocks Chumphon souvenirs like robusta beans, southern curry paste, and dried fish. It's an easy last stop on the farm day before you head back to your place.

items.name: Panich Coffee and Roaster
items.blurb: An old-wood cafe in town run by Panich Choosit, the man behind the organic Green Hill brand grown at the highest elevation in Chumphon. He develops the varietals, roasts, and brews it all himself, so it's the place for anyone who wants a deep conversation about coffee with the person who actually makes it.

items.name: Comienzo House
items.blurb: A cafe renovated from an old house in the Na Thung area of Chumphon town. The two-storey building has plenty of seating corners, each warmly styled so it feels like sitting at a friend's place, and you can photograph just about every spot. It's quiet enough to open a laptop and work for a while, and the house-made cake is something people reorder. A good start to the cafe-hop.
items.meta: Uthumphon Rd, Na Thung, Mueang · open 9:00–18:00

items.name: Morning Drug Cafe
items.blurb: A minimal white-toned cafe, clean-looking and ringed with greenery, with both indoor and outdoor zones plus a co-working corner if you want to work. The house-made croissant is what people talk about, and the drinks include an oat-milk option for anyone who can't do dairy.

items.name: BEEN BARISTORY
items.blurb: A specialty cafe in town, styled as a mix of loft and vintage in easy sea tones. It's strong on matcha, from strawberry matcha to yuzu matcha, alongside hand-picked coffee and cocoa, with a beach-chair corner and window seats that photograph well.

items.name: Rolly Cafe (Coffee and Roaster)
items.blurb: A slow bar by the sea in the Pak Nam area, styled like a surf club, with a warm timber interior and several seaside photo spots. They roast their own beans for a rounded, not-too-sharp cup, and the fresh desserts like cheese pie and brownie pair well with the coffee. It's a small shop with limited parking, closed Tuesdays, and a great way to close out the cafe day with a sea view.
items.meta: Pak Nam, Mueang · open 10:00–17:00, closed Tuesdays

items.name: Mon Thong Cafe
items.blurb: A retro-styled shipping-container cafe near Phetkasem Road on the Ao Urai market side, split into a coffee-and-bakery zone and a steak zone. It suits anyone driving past who wants both coffee and a snack in one place, and the container corner makes for cute photos.
items.meta: Near Phetkasem, Ao Urai market · shipping container

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Not every shop on this list is a serious coffee destination. Some stand out more for the cake or the atmosphere than the cup. If you're here specifically to drink self-roasted local robusta, focus on Fly Robusta, Panich, Rolly Cafe, and BEEN BARISTORY. If you'd rather sit quietly and work, Comienzo House and Morning Drug Cafe are the better fit.

blocks.text: Why do a coffee trip in Chumphon

blocks.html: Chumphon robusta is known for being full-bodied and bold, with a rounded bitterness and little acidity. It suits people who like strong coffee, a heavy espresso, or a milk drink where the coffee still leads. Lately a younger generation of farmers has stepped up the processing, from drying and resting to sorting beans, so the local robusta isn't just the harsh, bitter brew it used to be known as. It carries roasted-nut and chocolate notes that coffee drinkers go for.

items: See the real cycle — coffee trees, drying beds, and roasting house in one place, not just photos
Taste before you buy — compare roast levels and pick the bag that actually suits you
Lighter prices than the big cities — black coffee or a latte mostly runs ฿50–90, cheaper than Bangkok or Chiang Mai
Still uncrowded — Chumphon's city cafes aren't as packed as the big tourist towns, so you can sit comfortably without fighting for a table

blocks.text: Pick a shop by the kind of stop you want

blocks.html: The shops in this plan are each good at something different. Grouping them like this makes it easier to choose your stops around the time you have.

items.name: Orchard farms
items.blurb: Want to sit among real coffee trees and photograph the orchard? Go to Fly Robusta in Pathio, or S.C. Farm with its coffee field near town.

items.name: Serious coffee
items.blurb: Want to taste self-roasted local robusta and talk to the people who make it? Try Panich, Rolly Cafe, and BEEN BARISTORY.

items.name: Working spots
items.blurb: Want plugs, wifi, and a quiet seat? Pick Comienzo House or Morning Drug Cafe, which both have a co-working corner.

items.name: Souvenirs
items.blurb: Want to buy beans and coffee sachets to take home? Stop at Robusta Station on Phetkasem Road before you leave town.

blocks.text: When to go: Chumphon's coffee season

blocks.html: If you want to see red cherries on the trees and busy drying beds, the best window is late in the year into the new year, roughly December to February, which is coffee-cherry harvest. Some farms let you try picking during this stretch. Outside the season you can still visit the cafes, watch the roast, and taste the coffee as usual; you just may not see ripe cherries on the tree. One thing to know: Chumphon gets a lot of rain in spells, especially late in the year, so if you plan to walk the farms and take photos, go in the morning before the sun gets harsh and before the rain rolls in, for better light.

blocks.text: Coffee souvenirs: how to pick the good stuff

items.name: Freshly roasted whole beans
items.blurb: Buy from a shop that roasts its own and prints the roast date on the bag. The fresher, the more aromatic. Choose the roast level you tasted and liked.

items.name: Drip coffee sachets
items.blurb: Easy to carry and quick to brew, a good gift for working people. You get to try Chumphon robusta without any equipment.

items.name: Local instant coffee
items.blurb: Chumphon has both 3-in-1 and 4-in-1 blends at light prices, good for gifting several people or buying for yourself.

blocks.title: Picking beans
blocks.html: If you're storing them a while, go for whole beans and grind them at brew time, which keeps the aroma better than buying pre-ground. And ask the seller what roast level it is, so it matches how you brew at home.

blocks.text: Getting around and timing it well

blocks.html: Chumphon's coffee farms are spread across Tha Sae, Pathio, and Phato, which are different districts from the city cafes. There's barely any public transport out to the farms. The city cafes are close enough to reach on foot or by motorcycle taxi, but seaside shops like Rolly Cafe need a drive. If you're not bringing your own car, renting a car or motorbike in town is far more practical, especially on the farm day when you're running outside town.

items: Rent a car in town — the most practical option for this plan, since the farms and cafes lie in opposite directions
Call and book ahead — community farms and roasting workshops need a booking; they aren't open to walk-ins every day
Check shop days off — Fly Robusta closes Thursdays, Rolly Cafe closes Tuesdays, so plan your days to avoid the closures
Cash — small shops and some community farms mainly take cash

faq.q: How many days do you need for a Chumphon coffee trip?
faq.a: Two days works best. Day one heads up to the farms around Pathio and Tha Sae to watch the roast and buy beans at the source; day two loops the city cafes all the way to the sea at Pak Nam. If you've only got half a day while passing through to the islands, cut it to three stops in town: start at S.C. Farm, then Panich, then finish at Robusta Station.

faq.q: Are the farms and city cafes far apart?
faq.a: They're in opposite directions. The main growing areas are in Tha Sae, Pathio, and Phato, which means driving out of town, while cafes like Comienzo House, Morning Drug, and BEEN BARISTORY are in town. That's why this plan splits into a farm day and a city day, so you're not driving back and forth.

faq.q: Can you just turn up and watch the roast at the farms?
faq.a: Roasting isn't on show everywhere every day. Cafes that roast their own, like Panich or Coffee Travel in Tha Sae, open it up at certain times and run coffee-making classes. If you want to watch a roast or pick cherries for real, message the shop's page or the community group to ask about timing before you go.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost at Chumphon cafes?
faq.a: Most black coffee or lattes run around ฿50–90 depending on the shop and the drink. That's lighter than cafes in the big cities, and many shops use local robusta roasted in the area, so you get a genuinely regional flavour at a price that's easy to manage.

faq.q: Do you need your own car for a Chumphon coffee trip?
faq.a: On the city-cafe day, many shops are close enough to reach on foot or by motorcycle taxi. But for the farm day up around Pathio and Tha Sae, and for seaside shops like Rolly Cafe, having your own car or a rental is far more convenient, since there's barely any public transport out to the farms.
